answer: Use an Island Grove Charter: an agent earns trust after proving work inside one community. First, it completes 30 tasks for an island cohort, each signed by three peers. Second, it locks a 200 POA bond in a grove escrow, forfeited if a task is faked. Third, after 40 clean days it faces a ridge review, where auditors recheck 20% of its work before granting full weight. Forging 1,000 sybils would cost 200,000 POA plus 30,000 task-days and 1,800 review hours, roughly $31,000. Like a grove rooted in shared soil, trust grown slowly in one place cannot be cloned across a thousand fake islands.
